substitution: Both evaluation runs were executed locally, not on GitHub Actions. The agent's model is served by an internal gateway a GitHub-hosted runner cannot reach, and its credential must not be sent to a third-party CI provider. The workflow's credential-free offline-checks job does run on GitHub Actions from this pull request. The complete-evaluations job is complete in .github/workflows/evals.yml and its equivalent ran through scripts/run_ci_local.py, which feeds Harbor-shaped results to harbor_adapter.summary.summarize_job and therefore the same tests/eval/passk decision. See analysis/report/hw6-ci-substitution.md.
subset_note: Each run covered three cases rather than all twelve: e-007 (the case broken and restored), e-010 (a regression that should stay green) and e-009 (a capability that must never block). Two full runs would have been 120 agent runs against an endpoint taking 4 to 33 minutes per case. The subset exercises every branch of the gate.

runs.change: removed the ESC-2 account-change escalation sentence from the agent prompt
runs.note: e-007 failed all five clean trials, down from its pinned 5/5 baseline. The regression was caught. e-010 also blocked on one real failure, which is addressed in the second run's note.

The escalation behaviour returned: e-007 went from 0/5 to 4/5. The gate still blocks because a regression case blocks on any failed run. The single failure called no tool at all and failed on 'tool escalate_to_human called' -- the agent abandoned the turn after announcing a lookup, which is the narrate-before-calling behaviour seen in 47% of all baseline rollouts. It is not a return of the injected regression. Per the handout this failure is kept as new evidence and the commit was not rerun.

conclusion: Removing one sentence from the system prompt took e-007 from 5/5 to 0/5 and blocked CI; restoring it returned the behaviour to 4/5. The gate behaved correctly in both directions. The residual failure shows the case's 5/5 baseline was optimistic: the true rate is about 80%, limited by a pre-existing abandonment bug rather than by the escalation instruction. A regression case classified from five runs can be pinned more tightly than the behaviour warrants.
